name: Toyota Logistics Services Vehicle Distribution Center - Long Beach CA

fieldNotes.facilityType: Port of Long Beach vehicle processing & distribution center (TLS, ~180,000-200,000 vehicles/yr). Not a conventional dock warehouse — vehicles arrive by ro/ro ship at the Pier B wharf and by unit train on the rail spurs along the NE edge, are processed (accessory install, car wash, fuel) at the 155,000 sf processing building, and leave on auto-hauler trucks.
fieldNotes.truckGate: Whole property is inside a port-secure fenced perimeter (chain-link fence visible in Street View on every public-road edge; z20 sat shows a continuous fence line with marked lane crossings). Port of Long Beach maritime-security site (TWIC required, USCG oversight, random checks per construction-phase reporting) — controlled gated entry is certain.
fieldNotes.guardShack: Inferred true — TWIC-controlled maritime facilities have staffed gatehouses for vehicle ID/credential checks. A small gatehouse structure is consistent with the office cluster at the NW corner near the rail crossing, but a discrete guard booth could not be isolated in imagery; medium confidence.
fieldNotes.dockDoors: The processing building has a bank of dock-style doors along its NE face where auto-haulers and parts trailers load (a row of ~12-18 trailers is staged along that face in z18 imagery). Banded 10-25; this is a vehicle-processing site so 'dock doors' are atypical.
fieldNotes.dropArea: Vast — the entire site is effectively a vehicle marshalling yard; thousands of finished vehicles staged in striped lots. 'dropArea' as trailer stalls is less applicable, but auto-hauler/trailer drop capacity is large; banded 50+.
fieldNotes.railServed: Confirmed — multiple rail spurs run into the NE edge of the property; Street View shows tank/covered-hopper rail cars on the in-site track. TLS uses unit trains to distribute vehicles inland.
fieldNotes.scale: No truck scale identified; vehicle-processing ports typically do not weigh auto-haulers. Left false, flagged uncertain.
fieldNotes.fastLaneOpportunity: Wide paved aprons and multi-lane gate crossings at the rail-side entrance give ample room for an express/bypass lane.
fieldNotes.siteAreaAcres: Perimeter box ~62 acres covering the contiguous TLS fenced lots and processing buildings between Pico Ave / the rail corridor and the Pier B wharf.
fieldNotes.truckGateCount: At least one main rail-side gate plus a secondary lot access; estimated 2, flagged uncertain.
